column7: Control word: run, direction, reset, coast, quick stop.
column15: bit 0 = 0 = stop, 1 = run (operational); bit 1 = 0 = forward (clockwise), 1 = reverse; bit 2 = 1 = reset fault; bit 3 = 1 = coast to stop; bit 5 = 1 = quick stop (ramp 2); bit 6 = 1 = run at fixed frequency FF1; bit 7 = 1 = force the setpoint to 0

column7: Setpoint frequency, limited to the min/max frequency parameters.
Low byte = status bits, high byte = fault number.
column15: bit 0 = 1 = ready (READY); bit 1 = 1 = running (RUN); bit 2 = 0 = forward, 1 = reverse; bit 3 = 1 = fault (FAULT); bit 4 = 1 = actual frequency equals setpoint (0 = ramping); bit 5 = 1 = zero speed; bit 6 = 1 = speed control active; bit 7 = DA1: 0 = STO inhibit, 1 = STO ready; bit 8-15 = Fault word: the fault number (see notes), 0 = no fault

column7: Input states; the lowest bit is DI1.
Part-number code: frame size, voltage class, phases and power index as hex digits.
Selects where run commands and the speed reference come from.
column15: 0 = Terminal control; 1 = Digital reference, forward only; 2 = Digital reference, forward and reverse; 3 = PID controller; 4 = Fieldbus control (Modbus RTU if no fieldbus option); 5 = Server mode (follows a drive in client mode); 6 = CANopen control; 9 = SmartWire-DT control and speed reference; 10 = SmartWire-DT control, terminal speed reference; 11 = Terminal control, SmartWire-DT speed reference; 13 = SmartWire-DT control and reference, digital input enables
0 = No parity, 1 stop bit; 1 = No parity, 2 stop bits; 2 = Odd parity, 1 stop bit; 3 = Even parity, 1 stop bit

column7: Time without a valid telegram before P5-06 acts.

column15: 0 = Switch off (trip); 1 = Ramp to stop, then switch off; 2 = Ramp to stop, no fault; 3 = Run at fixed frequency 8 (P2-08)
0 = Ramps from drive parameters; 1 = Ramps from fieldbus
